summary: Two arrests that Fairbanks police recorded on Monday afternoon, a felony vehicle theft charge and a drink-driving charge, appeared on the daily bulletin only after it had twice been published as carrying nothing for the day; neither has a court file yet. The court's weekly filings report, re-run on Monday night, records 41 criminal cases filed at Fairbanks over the week to Oct. 19 and none at all on Monday itself, when court offices were closed for the Alaska Day observance. The Fairbanks court returned to a full calendar of 56 criminal cases on Tuesday. Court files in the Fairbanks mail theft case record fewer and different charges than were reported when the two defendants were arrested.

entries.title: Fairbanks woman arrested on a felony vehicle theft charge
body: A 49-year-old Fairbanks woman was arrested on the afternoon of Monday, Oct. 19 at the 700 block of 17th Avenue in Fairbanks, the Fairbanks Police Department daily bulletin records. The bulletin gives the time as 4:48 p.m. and the charge as vehicle theft in the first degree - taking a vehicle, aircraft or watercraft - which it records as a felony.

No court file has been opened behind the arrest. A search of the public case database returns no 2026 criminal case under the name, so the charge and the felony classification are those recorded by police rather than those filed by a prosecutor. She is arrested, not convicted, and the charge may be amended or not filed at all.
The arrest did not appear on the bulletin when the same page was read twice on Oct. 19, once in the early morning and once in the late afternoon. It was added afterwards.

sources.label: Fairbanks Police Department daily bulletin, Oct. 19

entries.title: Fairbanks man arrested on a drink-driving charge
body: A 37-year-old man was arrested at the 400 block of Merhar Avenue in Fairbanks at 3:46 p.m. on Monday, Oct. 19 on a charge of driving under the influence with a blood alcohol content of .08 per cent or more, which the Fairbanks Police Department daily bulletin records as a misdemeanour.
No court file has been opened behind the arrest, so the charge recorded by police is the only record of it. He is arrested, not convicted.

The police bulletin lists arrestees by first name, middle names and then surname. Read in that order the name on this arrest would be taken as a different surname; a search of the court's own party index establishes the surname as Custer.

sources.label: Fairbanks Police Department daily bulletin, Oct. 19

entries.title: Troopers report a theft investigation in Fairbanks, with charges expected
body: The Alaska State Troopers daily dispatch records that on Oct. 19 troopers received a report of a theft in Fairbanks, that the investigation is continuing and that charges are expected. The entry was posted at 7:48 p.m. that evening.
No person is named and no place more specific than the city is given. No charge has been filed.

sources.label: Alaska State Troopers daily dispatch, Oct. 19

entries.title: Court file in the Fairbanks mail theft case differs from the counts reported at the time of arrest
body: Two people were charged after Alaska State Troopers investigated a report of mail theft in Fairbanks on Oct. 17, in which troopers say they recovered stolen mail including an $8,000 life-insurance cheque, several driving licences and several credit cards, along with drug paraphernalia and controlled substances.

The trooper statement at the time, repeated in a news report dated Oct. 19, said that a 37-year-old man was charged with five felony counts and one misdemeanour count of theft plus a misdemeanour drug count, and that a 38-year-old woman was charged as an accessory to the thefts along with a felony drug count and a violation of conditions of release.

The court files record different charges. Case 4FA-26-02114CR charges Nolan Iver Peterson with two counts of theft in the second degree involving an access device or identification document, each a Class C felony, and one count of theft in the third degree of mail, a Class A misdemeanour - three counts in all, and no drug count appears on the file. Case 4FA-26-02117CR charges Julia Ann Pitka with six counts in her own name: misconduct involving a controlled substance in the third degree, a Class B felony; misconduct in the fifth degree, a Class A misdemeanour; two counts of theft in the second degree involving an access device or identification document, each a Class C felony; theft in the third degree of mail, a Class A misdemeanour; and violating a condition of release for a felony, a Class A misdemeanour. No accessory count is on her file.

An arrest report states what an officer alleged; the court file states what was charged. Both are charged, not convicted, and the charges may be amended or dismissed. Both cases are before the Fairbanks court, with preliminary hearings set for Oct. 28.

sources.label: Alaska State Troopers daily dispatch, Oct. 17

entries.title: Weekly criminal filings: 41 cases at Fairbanks, two at Delta Junction, none on the holiday Monday
body: The Alaska Court System's weekly report of criminal charges filed, run at 9:01 p.m. on Oct. 19 and covering Oct. 13 to Oct. 19, records 41 cases filed at the Fairbanks courthouse and two at Delta Junction. It records no cases at Nenana and none at Healy.

The Fairbanks cases run in an unbroken series from 4FA-26-02077CR to 4FA-26-02117CR. By filing day they are: Tuesday five, Wednesday eight, Thursday three, Friday twelve, Saturday four and Sunday nine. The report carries no filings for Monday, Oct. 19 at all. Court offices were closed that day for the Alaska Day observance, which fell on Sunday and was observed on the Monday.

The counts are the report's own for its own window. The report has previously been published without a case that had been filed on the last day of its window, so the figure for the most recent day should be read as a minimum.

The two Delta Junction cases are 4DJ-26-00064CR, in which no charging document has yet been filed, and 4DJ-26-00065CR, charging one count of permitting an unauthorised person to drive, an unclassified misdemeanour.

sources.label: Alaska Court System, criminal charges filed

entries.title: Fairbanks court back in session with 56 criminal cases calendared after the holiday
body: The Fairbanks court's daily public calendar for Tuesday, Oct. 20 carries 56 criminal cases, including an arraignment block of 23. On Monday, when court offices were closed for the Alaska Day observance, the whole Fairbanks calendar carried one case, heard by a weekend and holiday judge.

Among the matters set for today is a bail hearing at 11 a.m. in case 4FA-26-01818CR, listed in the calendar's comment field as concerning a proposed third-party custodian. The defendant is appearing from the Fairbanks Correctional Center.
Preliminary hearings are also set for 3:15 p.m. in cases 4FA-26-02063CR and 4NE-26-00103CR, and a calendar call at 1:30 p.m. in 4DJ-25-00014CR.

sources.label: Alaska Court System, Fairbanks daily public calendar, Oct. 20

entries.title: Three Nenana cases against one defendant calendared at Fairbanks, one for an offence recorded at Healy
body: Three criminal cases filed at the Nenana court are set for hearings at the Fairbanks courthouse at 11:30 a.m. on Tuesday, Oct. 20, all three against the same defendant, who is appearing from the Fairbanks Correctional Center. Two are motion hearings and one is a bail hearing.

Case 4NE-26-00086CR, filed Sep. 4, charges one count of assault in the fourth degree - recklessly injure, a Class A misdemeanour, flagged as domestic-violence related, with an offence location of Healy and an offence date of Sep. 3. Case 4NE-26-00092CR, filed Sep. 11, charges unlawful contact in breach of a court order, a Class A misdemeanour also flagged as domestic-violence related, and violating conditions of release for a misdemeanour, a Class B misdemeanour, both with an offence location of Fairbanks and an offence date of Sep. 9.
She is charged, not convicted. No victim is identified.

The weekly filings report records no cases at Healy, and has done so for 24 consecutive weeks. Healy has no criminal court of its own: offences recorded there are charged at Nenana or at Fairbanks, so a count of zero against the Healy court prefix is not a statement about the place.

sources.label: Alaska Court System, Fairbanks daily public calendar, Oct. 20

entries.title: No public safety column published for Monday
body: The Fairbanks Daily News-Miner's public safety report index carries 25 dated columns, the most recent dated Oct. 18. There is no column dated Oct. 19 or Oct. 20.
The column is the only local source that regularly carries the account behind a charge. Its Oct. 18 edition is behind a subscription wall after its first section heading.

sources.label: Fairbanks Daily News-Miner, public safety report index

entries.title: Fire crews called to an outside fire at North Pole and a vehicle fire in Fairbanks
body: The Fairbanks Emergency Communications Center dispatch feed records 42 incidents over roughly the 24 hours to early Tuesday. Among them were an outside fire at the 2740 block of Old Richardson Highway in North Pole at 1:06 a.m. on Oct. 20, cleared after 35 minutes with three units in attendance, and a vehicle fire on Carlton Drive in Fairbanks at 2:19 p.m. on Oct. 19, cleared after 16 minutes.
Seven fire alarms and one odour investigation were also dispatched. No traffic collision and no structure fire appears in the window.
The feed carries fire and medical dispatches only and has no police or crime category. Medical calls are not listed here.
